abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD). Yet, the physiological relationships linking age-related changes in peripheral biomarkers and measures of brain structure have only recently begun to be explored. Nonhuman primates, whose brains naturally express some of the pathologic hallmarks of AD/ADRD, including amyloid-beta (A{beta}) plaques, vascular amyloid, and neurofibrillary tangles, represent a critical translational bridge between rodent models and humans. Here, we utilized ultrasensitive multiplex assays and structural MRI to examine the relationship of plasma AD/ADRD biomarkers with age, sex, and whole brain cortical thickness (CT) and gray matter volume (GMV) in a cohort of chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes), humans' closest extant living relatives. Plasma levels (pg/ml) of total tau, phosphorylated tau 217 (pTau217), A{beta}40, A{beta}42, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and neurofilament light chain (NfL) were measured in a cross-sectional sample of 154 chimpanzees ranging from 12-57 years of age. As in humans, aging was associated with increased plasma total tau, pTau217, A{beta}40, A{beta}42, GFAP, and NfL levels, as well as reduced whole brain CT and GMV in chimpanzees. The ratio of plasma A{beta}42/A{beta}40 increased with age in male chimpanzees, whereas aging was not significantly associated with the ratio of pTau217/A{beta}42. Mediation analyses revealed that age-related increases in plasma A{beta}42 mediated whole brain GMV atrophy in chimpanzees. Together, these findings demonstrate that plasma AD/ADRD biomarkers and measures of brain structure undergo age-related changes in chimpanzees, which is highly relevant to the study of human aging and AD/ADRD.

metadata.title: Plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease reveal conserved features of age-related neurodegeneration in chimpanzees and humans

summary: In 154 chimpanzees aged 12-57, plasma AD biomarkers (tau, pTau217, Abeta40/42, GFAP, NfL) rose with age alongside brain atrophy, mirroring human aging.
title: Plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease reveal conserved features of age-related neurodegeneration in chimpanzees and humans
